title.narrative: A.O.6. Number of facilities established/strengthened

comment.narrative: 08-10-2021: All Palestinian institutions have shared their motivation to purchase the needed equipment to facilitate research and curricula development in the field of WASH and CSA through official motivation letters. ANNU will manage the procurement for all universities through their procurement department. The process will start in September, when all staff are back to work from their offices.

08-10-2021: An Najah University is leading the procurement of investment needs to all individual universities to comply with OKP guidelines. All universities have developed their shopping lists and motivation letters justifying the needs for the items they want to purchase. An Najah has assigned a procurement team the responsibility of implementing the process. Most of the goods were delivered to the recipient universities, and the process of receiving the gods by universities is still ongoing, which affected the payments process, we have a large number of pending payments that are not yet reported in R2 financial report. Procurement process has faced number of challenges imposed by COVID-19 pandemic and the Gaza war in May 2021. Vendors have encountered serious delays in shipments, which further delayed receiving lab equipment. Universities have used the investment funds to upgrade their labs to stimulate professors for new research areas, and involve more students in research projects. Other universities choose to use the investment funds for green houses, to practically demonstrate smart agriculture techniques Universities highly appreciate the investment fund part of the project because it covered funding shortage of the faculties to develop the labs and practical education

20-01-2023: 7 universities have their labs established/ upgraded: examples of investment items: 1. PPU: Total Organic Carbon Analyzer TOC-L CPN Standard/PC controlled. Portable Spectrophotometer 2. AAUP: Automatic Weather Station , The station consists of the following parts : with data logger model iMETOS 3.3 , with battery ,with solar panel to charge the battery , Smart greenhouse equipped with sensors and climatization equipment to deal and control the internal atmosphere in order to simualte furture climate changes. 4. Hebron University: Advanced fertigation control system. 5. PTUK: a) DRY BLOCK digesters for kjeldahl with scrubber and vacuum pump, Velp DK-8, Italy - with all accessories. b) ASTREE Electronic Tongue upgrade parts , ASTREE V5 upgrade kit (sensor set#6 included) 6. AQU: Nicolet iS20 Mid-Infrared FT-IR Spectrophotometer and software, Model: TN912A0968. 7. An Najah: Establishment of modern greenhouse equipped with all needed facilities for soiless cultivation. 8. Islamic University: Genesys 50 Dual (Split) Beam Single Cell UV-Visible Scanning Spectrophotometer, THS840-313900, ThermoScientific. 9. Azhar Univerity: Desalination Unit.

title.narrative: A.S.4. Number of SMEs supported

comment.narrative: 08-10-2021: The project has started working on students’ entrepreneurship competition. The student can come up with entrepreneurship idea in WASH and CSA. During the process, the entrepreneurship expert will provide a guidance to the students. The project will support for the four best entrepreneurship model for the start-up. The competition process starts by forming a committee to set the competition criteria to be officially announced to students, professors will walk students through their work and get them ready for the competition.

08-10-2021: The project has worked on two parallel tracks towards developing entrepreneurship concepts and practices. The project has worked with TU delft university in developing the professors and administrators' capacities in entrepreneurship, developed the entrepreneurship curricula to teach students, and organized an entrepreneurship competition to help students grasp the learning and acquire the entrepreneurial skills. The competition aims to deliver training, coaching, and mentorship services to student entrepreneurs and alumni of Palestianian universities (Bachelors, Masters, and PhD levels) aiming to establish their startups in the WASH and CSA sectors. The proposed initiative--in conjunction with the Delft Center for Entrepreneurship and a consortium of Palestinain universities and participants--is designed to meet with the following project objectives: ● Increasing awareness of social entrepreneurship through each phase of the program. ● Breaking down theoretical barriers and difficulties in the Arab and Palestinian entrepreneurial environment in general and in the water and agriculture sectors in particular. ● Capacity building for the entrepreneurs, stimulating creativity and promoting the concept of social impact in both design and measurement. ● Offering an extensive curriculum in lean startup, customized mentorship and consultancy, in addition to follow-up and pitch-day preparations. ● Building a virtual community of alumni social entrepreneurs in the water and agriculture sectors. TU Delft with a local consultant BEDAR has developed the concept of the competition, prepared the promotion strategy of the competition, and finalized the application to be posted on universities' websites to reach to the largest number of students. Four Award winners will be declared by the competition event, whose startups will be incubated in the Palestinian universities business incubators for further support after the project ends.

20-01-2023: OKP has launched Entreprenureship competetion in WASH & CSA. 62 teams/ students applied for the competetion from 9 different universites. 25 teams/ students were selected for the training. 15 innovative buisness ideas run for the final competetion, where 4 winners will be announced. These 15 buisness ideas filled the gaps in WASH & CSA with artificial inteligence elements. One example is cultivation of mushrooms (champaign mushrooms). Mushroom is a not normally grown in Palestine, therefore is imported from Israel at high cost. The team has worked on growing mushrooms in certain circumstances to make the mushroom available at affordable rates. Another idea was to create an application to connect farmers with local market, traders and interested labor forces. The application helped farmers to promote their products and improve their income. It also helped unemployed youth to find jobs easily. An echo friendly startup was to convert organic house wastes into organic fertilizers that can be used to improve agriculture, it also helped households to get rid of their organic wastes in an envoironment friendly fashion.

27-07-2023: Entrepreneurial training program: Under the Orange Knowledge Program (OKP), an entrepreneurial training program was implemented for students, facilitated by a consulting firm. The program involved a business development boot camp, which equipped students with essential skills and knowledge related to entrepreneurship, including idea pitching, business planning, and market analysis.
As a result of the training program, a total of 10 student teams qualified for the entrepreneurial challenge held in September 2022. The challenge provided a platform for these teams to showcase their innovative business ideas and compete for recognition and support. To ensure impartiality and industry relevance, a jury consisting of private sector companies and stakeholders, nominated by the project, was responsible for overseeing the entrepreneurial challenge.
After a rigorous evaluation process, four student companies were awarded for their exceptional ideas, potential for growth, and viability. These awards recognize the entrepreneurial spirit and efforts of the students, providing them with encouragement, validation, and support to further develop their business ventures.
The involvement of private sector companies and stakeholders in the jury panel signifies the commitment of the project to bridge the gap between academia and the business world. By engaging these industry representatives, the entrepreneurial challenge ensures that the participating student companies receive valuable feedback, mentorship, and potential networking opportunities with key players in their respective industries.
The entrepreneurial training and challenge implemented by OKP create an environment that fosters innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship among students. By equipping them with the necessary skills and providing a platform to showcase their ideas, OKP contributes to the cultivation of a vibrant and dynamic entrepreneurial ecosystem within the partner universities.

comment.narrative:
27-07-2023: Better Performance HEI: A better performance Higher Education Institution (HEI) after benefiting from the Orange Knowledge Program (OKP) is defined as partner institution that has undergone positive transformations and achieved notable improvements in various aspects of its operations, educational quality, and overall impact. This definition encompasses the following key elements:
Enhanced Educational Quality: A better performing HEI demonstrates improvements in the quality of its educational programs and services. After receiving the updated curricula, research opportunities, enhanced physical education environment through OKP interventions. This includes updated and relevant curricula, innovative teaching methods, and improved learning outcomes. The institution places a strong emphasis on student-centered approaches, fostering critical thinking, practical skills development, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
Strengthened Research and Innovation Capacities: OKP support enables HEIs to strengthen their research and innovation capacities. A better performing HEI has an increased research output, with a focus on relevant and impactful projects that contribute to addressing societal challenges. The institution promotes a research culture, fosters interdisciplinary collaboration, and establishes partnerships with other universities, research centers, and industry stakeholders.
Internationalization and Global Engagement: Through the OKP, HEIs gain opportunities for international cooperation and knowledge exchange. A better performing HEI actively engages in international collaborations, joint research projects, and student and staff mobility programs. It establishes partnerships with renowned universities and institutions worldwide, fostering a global outlook, cross-cultural understanding, and exposure to diverse perspectives.

title.narrative: B.O.4. Number of organisations developed and implemented a gender strategy

comment.narrative: 08-10-2021: An Najah University has recently developed a gender policy among the internal policies of its system. An Najah has learnt from the COCA assessment that has been conducted y Nuffic to draft a gender policy to ensure the attainment of gender equality in the organization by redressing the existing gender imbalances. It also provides for equal opportunities for women and men to actively participate and contribute to their fullest ability and equitably benefit from national development. The development of this Policy has been necessitated by a number of donors and international community actors as well as internal forces called for a gender policy stimulating women's participation to combat increasing gender based violence and gender disparities in positions of decision making.
